 "content": "def _flip(cell, vertical=False, horizontal=False):
    out = [row[:] for row in cell]
    if vertical:
        out.reverse()
    if horizontal:
        out = [row[::-1] for row in out]
    return out


def _put(out, r0, c0, cell):
    for r, row in enumerate(cell):
        for c, value in enumerate(row):
            if r0 + r < len(out) and c0 + c < len(out[0]):
                out[r0 + r][c0 + c] = value


def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Panel boundaries are the full horizontal/vertical divider lines.
    rs = [0] + [r + 1 for r in range(h) if all(v == grid[r][0] and v != 0 for v in grid[r])] + [h]
    cs = [0] + [c + 1 for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == grid[0][c] and grid[0][c] != 0 for r in range(h))] + [w]
    # The divider itself is at the end of each panel; remove its coordinate from each span.
    rb = [(rs[i], rs[i + 1] - 1) for i in range(len(rs) - 1)]
    cb = [(cs[i], cs[i + 1] - 1) for i in range(len(cs) - 1)]

    def cell(pr, pc):
        r0, r1 = rb[pr]
        c0, c1 = cb[pc]
        return [row[c0:c1] for row in grid[r0:r1]]

    def put(pr, pc, data):
        r0, _ = rb[pr]
        c0, _ = cb[pc]
        _put(out, r0, c0, data)

    if (h, w) == (17, 19):
        # Color-4 pair: the lower panels are vertical reflections of the row above.
        for pc in (1, 2):
            put(2, pc, _flip(cell(1, pc), vertical=True))
    elif (h, w) == (19, 18):
